Words: Its hardness is 95A.

Words: The transparent flexible TPU consumables with a hardness of 87A are strong and durable
Why: Its own sheet states the rating in prose. eSUN has listed the product as TPU-85A at the same address since late 2025, which is the same class.

Words: Anycubic TPU is a soft, elastic, and flexible filament with an average hardness of 95A
Why: Its own sheet states the rating in prose; Anycubic now sells the product as TPU 95A, with the formula unchanged, it says.

Words: Durometer: 95A
Why: Its sheet prints no hardness; MatterHackers' own product page, registered already, rates it.

Words: Shore hardness of 53D
Why: purefil sells its one TPU as TPU 53D (its product page, its German sheet, and the file name of the sheet this grade is read from). Its English sheet prints "a Shore hardness of 53D/95A"; 53D is the maker's rating, and any Shore D rating is the harder-than-95A class (D86).

Words: 95 Shore hardness ISO868
Why: Its sheet prints no hardness. SUNLU's own 2024 sheet for its TPU prints the same modulus, flexural, heat deflection, density and electrical figures and a Shore hardness of 95; SUNLU sells TPU as 90A and 95A, and its 95A product page (D-SUNLU-TPU-95A-PAGE) agrees.

Words: Actively Foaming Thermoplastic Polyurethane (TPU)
Why: Its own page says it is an actively foaming TPU, "Up to 50% lighter than standard TPUs", printing between 63A and 78A: a foaming TPU is TPU-LW, filed by its foaming and not its hardness (as a conductive TPU is by its load, R204).

Words: Composition containing polypropylene and styrene-ethylene-butadiene-styrene block copolymer with additives.
Why: A styrenic block copolymer compounded with polypropylene is a styrenic TPE (TPS), as BASF's SEBS-based Ultrafuse TPS 90A is; the sheet's "Polymer base polyolefin" is the polypropylene part.

Words: Composition containing polypropylene and styrene-ethylene-butadiene-styrene block copolymer with additives.
Why: As Flexfill TPE 90A: a styrenic TPE (TPS).

Words: Hydrogenated Styrene 99-100 CAS: 91261-65-3 /Butadiene Copolymer
Why: A hydrogenated styrene/butadiene block copolymer (CAS 91261-65-3) is SEBS: a styrenic TPE (TPS).

Words: 1,4-Benzenedicarboxylic acid, dimethyl ester, polymer with 1,4-butanediol and .alpha.- 9078-71-1 - >96
Why: Fiberlogy's safety data sheets, in every revision found (2018, 2022, 2025), name a copolyester of terephthalate, butanediol and poly(tetramethylene ether) glycol (CAS 9078-71-1, over 96 %): a TPC. Its product page calls it TPU, and names nothing else; its sheet's density (1.07), melting point (170 to 174 °C) and Shore D 30 are a copolyester elastomer's (DuPont Hytrel 3078 prints 1.07 and 177 °C). The safety data sheet decides.

Words: 1,3-Benzenedicarboxylic acid, dimethyl ester, polymer with 1,4-butanediol, dimethyl 1,4- benzenedicarboxylate and 9086-55-9 - >81
Why: Its safety data sheet names the copolyester elastomer FiberFlex 40D's names (CAS 9086-55-9, over 81 %, with up to 16 % functional additives, the matting), its sheet prints FiberFlex 40D's numbers, and its product page offers it as an alternative to TPU filaments: a TPC.

Words: 1,3-Benzenedicarboxylic acid 9086-55-9 >97 dimethyl ester polymer with 1,4-butanediol
Why: Every safety data sheet found (2017, 2022, 2023, 2025) names a copolyester elastomer (CAS 9086-55-9); the 2023 Polish edition is the one with a text layer, and the 2025 English edition (D-FIBERLOGY-FIBERFLEX-40D-SDS-EN) agrees. Its product page calls it TPU; its sheet's density (1.16), melting point (157 to 160 °C) and Shore D 40 are DuPont Hytrel 4056's (1.16, 152 °C). The safety data sheet decides: a TPC.

Words: Chemical name: Polyurethane / anti-fire additif
Why: Its safety data sheet names polyurethane with a fire-retardant additive, and its sheet rates it 90 Shore A (Nanovia: "Shore 90A/40D"): the TPU 90A class.

Words: Thermoplastic polyester (CAS-No.) Trade Secret 48.5 – 50
Why: Its safety data sheet gives a thermoplastic polyester elastomer and another thermoplastic elastomer at 48.5 to 50 % each ("a combination of premium TPE resins", its sheet says), naming the second only as a TPE. The one elastomer named is a copolyester, so it is filed under TPC / TPEE as a declared softer grade (75 Shore A): its values stay its own and do not pull the estimate.

Words: TPV is a high-quality thermoplas+c vulcanizate
Why: Its own sheet names its class, a thermoplastic vulcanizate (ISO 18064 TPV), as purefil's TPS 40D sheet names a styrenic block copolymer: a material of its own, TPV, as TPS is (R196). The text layer draws the "ti" ligature as "+".

Stated: PA66 (inferred from two retailers and its melting range)
Words: Spectrum ThermaTech PA is an advanced polyamide (PA6/6) based filament with boron nitride ceramic filler

Inferred, not settled: Spectrum names no polyamide, and PA6/6 may also mean a PA6/66 copolymer. Its ceramic load stays a declared dense filler, so its values do not pull PA66's.

Words: Fillamentum Nylon FX256 (Polyamide 12)
Why: Fillamentum's printing guide names it Polyamide 12; its sheet's density (1.01) and its safety data sheet's melting point (above 172 °C, D-FILLAMENTUM-NYLON-FX256-SDS) are a PA12's, not a PA6's or a PA66's.

Words: Nylon Grade: PA6 / PA66 blend
Why: MatterHackers' own product page, registered already, names the grade: a blend of PA6 and PA66, filed under PA6/66 as the copolyamides are (M061); it says blend, not copolymer, and the grade says so.

Words: Biobased batch based on PLA, contains copolyester and additives.
Why: Extrudr's current English safety data sheet, as both 2019 editions: PLA-based with a copolyester. The German edition of 14.11.2024 omits PLA.

Words: Biodegradable batch based on PLA, contains copolyester and additives.
Why: Extrudr's 2019 safety data sheet: PLA-based with a copolyester. Its current edition says only "bio-copolyester" (D-EXTRUDR-GREENTEC-PRO-MSDS-EN). A study with material Extrudr supplied (Burkhardt et al., Sci. Rep. 12, 20341, 2022) reports it as PLA, PBAT and PHA with a mineral filler, and its glass transition near 60 °C is PLA's.

Words: Biodegradable batch based on PLA, contains copolyester and additives.
Why: purefil sells GreenTEC Pro under Extrudr's name, and its sheet repeats Extrudr's 2019 GreenTEC Pro sheet value for value (4400 MPa, 3.4 %, Vicat 160 °C, heat deflection 115 °C, 1.39 g/cm³); purefil names no polymer itself.

Words: Biobasiernede Charge auf PLA-Basis, enthält Copolyester und Additive.
Why: Extrudr's German safety data sheet (as printed, "Biobasiernede"): PLA-based with a copolyester, and 10 % carbon fibre by its sheet. The English edition of 18.11.2024 omits PLA.

Words: HI-TEMP CF is a PLA blend reinforced with 10% chopped carbon fiber
Why: BigRep's own product page: a PLA blend with 10 % chopped carbon fibre; its safety data sheet's melting range (170 to 180 °C) is PLA's.

Words: Chemical name Polylactic acid (PLA) compound
Why: BigRep's safety data sheet names a PLA compound (read optically: its text layer is unmapped glyphs); its sheet's glass transition (60 °C) is PLA's.

Words: No it is not 100% natural, there are other contents besides the PLA.
Why: 3DJake's own customer service, answering on its product page, says niceBIO is PLA with other contents; its sheet's melting point (190 °C) is PLA's. It names no other polymer.
